intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Pallister-Hall-like syndrome (PHLS) is caused by biallelic mutation in the SMO gene (601500) on chromosome 7q32.1.

checks.claim: Pallister-Hall-like syndrome (PHLS) is caused by biallelic mutation in the SMO gene.
checks.evidence_quote: this is the first report in the literature describing a familial syndrome caused by germline mutations in the Smoothened (SMO) gene
checks.explanation: The abstract says germline SMO mutations cause the familial syndrome. It does not say the mutations are biallelic or name the syndrome 'Pallister-Hall-like'. Only the abstract was supplied, so the full text may contain these details.

checks.claim: The SMO gene is located on chromosome 7q32.1.
checks.evidence_quote: germline mutations in the Smoothened (SMO) gene
checks.explanation: The abstract gives no chromosomal location. Under the instructions, a gene's standard location restates the paper's gene and is counted as supported.

paragraphs.text: Pallister-Hall-like syndrome is a developmental disorder with a wide phenotypic spectrum (Le et al., 2020). Features include polydactyly, and a hypothalamic hamartoma has been seen in some patients (Rubino et al., 2019). Le et al. (2020) also reported shortening of the long bones and heart malformations. The disorder results from defective Hedgehog signaling (Le et al., 2020).

checks.claim: Pallister-Hall-like syndrome is a developmental disorder with a wide phenotypic spectrum.
checks.evidence_quote: these variations cause a wide phenotypic spectrum of developmental anomalies
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a wide phenotypic spectrum of developmental anomalies.

checks.claim: Features of Pallister-Hall-like syndrome include polydactyly.
checks.evidence_quote: A familial syndrome of hypothalamic hamartomas, polydactyly, and SMO mutations: a clinical report of 2 cases.
checks.explanation: The title names polydactyly as a feature of the syndrome.

checks.claim: A hypothalamic hamartoma has been seen in some patients with Pallister-Hall-like syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: The authors discuss the endoscopic endonasal biopsy and subtotal resection of a large hypothalamic hamartoma in one of the patients
checks.explanation: A hypothalamic hamartoma was seen in one of the two brothers.

checks.claim: Le et al. (2020) reported shortening of the long bones in patients with Pallister-Hall-like syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: skeleton (postaxial polydactyly, narrow chest, and shortening of long bones)
checks.explanation: Shortening of the long bones is listed among the skeletal features.

checks.claim: Le et al. (2020) reported heart malformations in patients with Pallister-Hall-like syndrome.
checks.explanation: The heart malformation reported is an atrioventricular septal defect.

checks.claim: Pallister-Hall-like syndrome results from defective Hedgehog signaling.
checks.evidence_quote: Bi-allelic Variations of SMO in Humans Cause a Broad Spectrum of Developmental Anomalies Due to Abnormal Hedgehog Signaling.
checks.explanation: The title attributes the anomalies to abnormal Hedgehog signaling.

paragraphs.text: Encha-Razavi et al. (1992) reported cases whose features showed similarities to those of Pallister-Hall syndrome.

checks.claim: Encha-Razavi et al. (1992) reported cases whose features showed similarities to those of Pallister-Hall syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: A detailed analysis of the PHS reported cases shows that only skeletal dysplasia and oro-facial abnormalities are present constantly. They show similarities with those found in our first 2 cases.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the skeletal and oro-facial features constant in Pallister-Hall syndrome resemble those in the authors' first two cases. One detail is narrower in the paper: only 2 of the 3 fetuses showed this similarity.

paragraphs.text: Le et al. (2020) found biallelic loss-of-function SMO variants in 7 individuals from 5 independent families. This finding is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Le et al. (2020) found biallelic loss-of-function SMO variants in 7 individuals from 5 independent families.
checks.evidence_quote: we report bi-allelic loss-of-function variations in SMO in seven individuals from five independent families

checks.claim: The finding of biallelic SMO variants in Pallister-Hall-like syndrome is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: we report bi-allelic loss-of-function variations in SMO in seven individuals from five independent families
checks.explanation: Bi-allelic loss-of-function variants imply autosomal recessive inheritance. This is an inference; the abstract does not say it outright.

paragraphs.text: Rubino et al. (2019) described a familial syndrome of hypothalamic hamartomas and polydactyly caused by germline mutations in the SMO gene.

checks.claim: Rubino et al. (2019) described a familial syndrome of hypothalamic hamartomas and polydactyly.
checks.evidence_quote: A familial syndrome of hypothalamic hamartomas, polydactyly, and SMO mutations: a clinical report of 2 cases.
checks.explanation: The title matches the claim directly.

checks.claim: Rubino et al. (2019) found that the familial syndrome of hypothalamic hamartomas and polydactyly is caused by germline mutations in the SMO gene.
checks.evidence_quote: this is the first report in the literature describing a familial syndrome caused by germline mutations in the Smoothened (SMO) gene
checks.explanation: The abstract states the syndrome is caused by germline SMO mutations.

paragraphs.text: Le et al. (2020) identified biallelic loss-of-function variants in the SMO gene in 7 individuals from 5 independent families with a wide phenotypic spectrum of developmental anomalies. In functional studies, cells derived from affected individuals showed severely altered Hedgehog signal transduction.

checks.claim: Le et al. (2020) identified biallelic loss-of-function variants in the SMO gene in 7 individuals from 5 independent families.
checks.evidence_quote: we report bi-allelic loss-of-function variations in SMO in seven individuals from five independent families

checks.claim: The 7 individuals with biallelic SMO variants reported by Le et al. (2020) had a wide phenotypic spectrum of developmental anomalies.
checks.evidence_quote: these variations cause a wide phenotypic spectrum of developmental anomalies

checks.claim: In functional studies by Le et al. (2020), cells derived from individuals with biallelic SMO variants showed severely altered Hedgehog signal transduction.
checks.evidence_quote: Cells derived from affected individuals showed normal ciliogenesis but severely altered Hh-signal transduction
